paragraphs.en: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now? And anyway-aren't they all closing?

chunks.zh: 问起公共图书馆，人们脑海里就会浮现某种形象

chunks.en: dusty, old-fashioned,
chunks.zh: 落满灰尘、老气横秋

chunks.en: the sort of place you enjoyed as a child
chunks.zh: 那是小时候很喜欢的地方

chunks.en: but, rather like a British seaside town,

chunks.en: would you go there now?
chunks.zh: 你现在还会去吗

sentences.translation: 一提起公共图书馆，人们脑海里就会浮现这样的形象：落满灰尘、老气横秋，小时候很喜欢，但就像英国的海滨小镇一样，你现在还会去吗？

sentences.translation: 再说了，它们不都在关门吗？

paragraphs.en: The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday. As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald's.

paragraphs.en: Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity, while books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.

sentences.en: Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity, while books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.

chunks.zh: 虽然图书现在是、也永远应该是图书馆的核心

sentences.translation: 走进任何一家图书馆，你都会看到一派繁忙景象；图书现在是、也永远应该是图书馆的核心，但这里还提供就业咨询、语言课程、数字资源使用及相关支持等许多其他服务。

words.meaning: 使用数字资源或设备的机会

paragraphs.en: There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs. Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP's surgery, there are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.

paragraphs.en: In return for all of this, you'll be asked for precisely nothing. There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself, you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not. There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same. Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated. There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.

paragraphs.en: The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed. An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England. It is, of course, 230 libraries too many. So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.

paragraphs.en: The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children. If we don't use them, we will end up losing them. And for those who haven't been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.
